method: Each persona walks the real pages in Chrome, cold, at their own screen size, trying the task they would come with. Every grade cites findings from that walk. Three personas are held out: they are graded every round but never used to choose a fix, so a rise in their grades is evidence the fixes are general rather than fitted.

axes.name: First-open value
axes.asks: Opening the example, does the value leap out within a minute, and does it make me want to drill in?

axes.name: Process clarity
axes.asks: Do I always know where I am, what happens next, and why I am being asked?

axes.name: Effort to express intent
axes.asks: Is getting my meaning in, and settling what is open, fast and natural for someone like me?

axes.name: Trust and honesty
axes.asks: Is every claim checkable, every source shown, and nothing overstated, including sample data?

axes.name: Depth on demand
axes.asks: Can I drill from any summary to the exact statement, rule, part, journey or file behind it?

axes.name: Craft and access
axes.asks: Is it well made, readable and accessible: layout, type, contrast, phone, keyboard, screen reader?

axes.name: Openness and extensibility
axes.asks: Can I see how it works, extend its rules and parts, integrate its outputs, and contribute?

personas.name: Denise Harper
personas.role: Director of Student Success at a community college
personas.tech: Uses the student information system daily; has never written code
personas.comesTo: Get a tool built that warns students before a missed bill becomes a crisis, without waiting a year for IT
dealBreakers: anything that looks like it will embarrass her in front of IT

personas.name: Raj Mehta
personas.tech: Writes PRDs and acceptance criteria; reads code a little
personas.comesTo: Turn a PRD into something engineering cannot misread, and see the acceptance tests before sprint planning
values: export to tools his team uses
dealBreakers: a process slower than writing the ticket

personas.name: Lena Okafor
personas.comesTo: Find out what it would take to build her scheduling app and what it would cost to keep honest
values: what already exists versus what is new

personas.name: Tom Brennan
personas.tech: Twenty years shipping; skeptical of AI code generation
personas.comesTo: Find the hole: where does the model get to decide, and what stops it shipping wrong code
dealBreakers: demo data dressed as real results

personas.name: Aiko Sato
personas.comesTo: Judge whether the experience is crafted, and whether feel words like calm survive to the build

personas.name: Grace Liu
personas.comesTo: See whether the journeys and coverage would actually catch defects, and how many tests she would get

personas.name: Marcus Reed
personas.comesTo: Decide whether anything built this way could pass his review
dealBreakers: anything sent to a model without saying so

personas.name: Dr. Priya Raman
personas.role: Research scientist, evaluations team at an AI lab
personas.tech: Designs evals, studies reward hacking and specification gaming
personas.comesTo: Judge whether this is a real contribution to specification and evaluation, or a nice UI over prompts

personas.name: Sam Whitaker
personas.role: Partner, seed and Series A fund focused on developer tools and AI
personas.tech: Former PM; sees forty AI dev-tool pitches a month
personas.comesTo: Decide in five minutes whether there is a wedge and a moat
dealBreakers: having to be walked through it
looks like every other agent tool

personas.name: Jordan Ellis
personas.tech: Maintains widely used libraries; reviews licences and governance
personas.comesTo: See whether this is genuinely open: licence, source, formats, and whether outsiders can extend it
dealBreakers: open core with the useful part closed

personas.name: Rosa Delgado
personas.role: Accessibility consultant; low vision, uses a screen reader and 200% zoom
personas.comesTo: Find out whether a non-sighted or low-vision person can state intent and sign it

personas.name: Kenji Watanabe
personas.role: Manufacturing engineering manager at an automotive supplier
personas.comesTo: Check whether the manufacturing vocabulary is used correctly or just borrowed
values: correct use of datum, balloon, control plan, BOM, make or buy
dealBreakers: metaphors that break under an engineer's reading

personas.name: Keisha Moore
personas.role: Community health worker who would use an app built this way
personas.comesTo: A colleague sent her the example link: does she understand what it is and whether it would help her clients
